channel.title: What the AI!? by Kunal Mukherjee
channel.description: AI explained for the people who run things.

item.title: Build your AI superpowers #1: Goblin Tools
item.description: Every Saturday, one AI tool and one new superpower. First up: Goblin Tools, which turns overwhelming tasks into small, doable steps.

item.title: The Trust Economy: why marketers must care who owns the AI
item.description: From cool copy to brand safety. Why trust and data sovereignty are the new currency, two prompts to audit your stack, and India's sovereign AI toolkit.

item.title: The death of the rectangle: when AI opens its eyes
item.description: The screenless revolution. Why your camera is the new keyboard, the rise of AI for blue-collar work, and how vision AI turns every mechanic into a master technician.

item.title: The Forever Interface: when AI becomes memory
item.description: Dedicated to my father. The shift from AI that does tasks to AI that offers presence: digital ancestry, family clouds and passing wisdom forward.

item.title: The end of static media: the movie is now an app
item.description: Software is eating the studio. Elastic cinema, AI-made micro-dramas from Tier 2 India, and why the creative technologist is the hybrid to become.

item.title: The Doing Era: why 2026 changes everything
item.description: 2026 is the year AI stops chatting and starts doing. From prompting to delegating, the rise of the one-person unicorn, and India's leap to voice agents.

item.title: The end of the Information Tax
item.description: For 75 years India has paid an information tax. How AI moves us from search to synthesis, and why in India it is about access, not efficiency.

item.title: AI does not level the playing field. It widens the gap
item.description: Prompt copiers, tool tourists and quiet operators. Four AI workflows every marketer should master, and why India could become the capital of AI-led marketing.

item.title: You're overthinking AI. Here's what actually matters
item.description: AI won't steal your job, it will steal your excuses. Why judgment, not output, is your real edge, plus a Chief of Staff prompt and five underrated tools.
